taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: most plants 30 cm to 50 cm high, under FEIS's maximum, as in the photos.

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): "a native, drought-deciduous, microphyllous shrub growing up to 1.65 feet (50 cm) tall".

traits.age_max_years.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): "It has an observed longevity of about 50 years".

traits.life_span.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): "relatively short lived for a desert shrub", about 50 years: a perennial.

traits.woodiness.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): "a native, drought-deciduous, microphyllous shrub".

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): "drought-deciduous"; "Most new leaves ... develop and mature during the winter and early spring".

traits.rosette.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): "Innumerable slender and brittle branches spring up from the base forming a compact, roughly hemispherical crown": leaves along the branches, no rosette.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Leaves alternate along the twigs, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 212351627, 18473955, 157623372, 265471097, 158201416, 156980924, 202338997, 214504237): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_division.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 946), Franseria deltoidea: leaves distinctly petioled, the blades serrate or serrulate: simple, undivided blades.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 946), Franseria deltoidea: blades serrate or serrulate, not lobed or dissected as in its relatives.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): "Leaf length is 0.6 to 0.8 inches (1.5-2 cm) or smaller".

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: blades about half as wide as long, 5 mm to 1 cm, triangular-lanceolate as in the photos.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: petioles 3 mm to 8 mm; Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 946) call the leaves distinctly petioled.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Blades triangular (deltate) to triangular-lanceolate, as the name says, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 212351627, 18473955, 157623372, 265471097, 158201416, 156980924, 202338997, 214504237): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 946), Franseria deltoidea: leaf blades serrate or serrulate.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): "The branches and young leaves ... are tomentulose and resinous. Leaves become glabrous above with age".

traits.leaf_hairs_beneath.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 946), Franseria deltoidea: leaves canescent-tomentulose beneath, green above.

traits.inflorescence.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): "Staminate heads are borne terminally. Two-flowered, pistillate involucres are clustered below the staminate spikes".

traits.inflorescence_unit.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): staminate heads in terminal spikes: the units are capitula.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: staminate spikes 2 cm to 6 cm long, as in the photos.

traits.disc_colour.note: Small heads greenish yellow; sRGB by eye, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 212351627, 18473955, 157623372, 265471097, 158201416, 156980924, 202338997, 214504237): the sources read give no count or measure. Stated as the disc florets' colour, as its heads are discoid (it was flower_colour, which a capitulum does not have).

traits.flowering_position.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): "Staminate heads are borne terminally".

traits.sexual_system.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): staminate heads in spikes and pistillate involucres clustered below them on the same plant: monoecious.

traits.fruit_type.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): "They produce globose, spiny achenes".

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 946), Franseria deltoidea: fruit turbinate, about 6 mm long, 2- or 3-beaked.

traits.fruit_armature.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 946), Franseria deltoidea: the bur with about 20 or more flattened, often hook-tipped spines.

traits.flowering_months.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 948), Franseria deltoidea: very abundant on plains and mesas in Maricopa, Pinal and Pima Counties, December to April (FEIS gives February to July across its range).

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: burs ripe from March to May, after the winter flowering; FEIS says seeds come after both summer and winter rains.

traits.elevation_min_m.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): "grows from 1,000 to 3,000 feet (300-900 m)".

traits.elevation_max_m.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): "grows from 1,000 to 3,000 feet (300-900 m)"; Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 948) give 1,000 to 2,800 feet.

traits.moisture.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): "commonly grows in open spaces on pediments, upper bajada surfaces, and basin floors": dry desert ground.

traits.light.note: FEIS species review, Ambrosia deltoidea (Marshall 1994): "a dominant or codominant member of the Arizona Upland Subdivision of the Sonoran Desert" that "commonly grows in open spaces".

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a low, compact, rounded shrub of many brittle grey stems from the base, grey-green triangular leaves, short spikes of small greenish heads at the twig tips.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for triangle-leaf bursage from its sources and the photos the traits cite, on the template of white bursage (ambrosia-dumosa); the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.4 m tall at 12 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows on a Sonoran Desert bajada. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Saguaro desert scene (west bajada, Tucson Mountain District, 2026-10-19): sizes and forms from FEIS, Kearney and Peebles (1942) and Abrams, counts and colours from iNaturalist photos, drawing values from the library's rules for the form.
